title: JCM v1.0: A Differentiable, Intermediate-Complexity Atmospheric Model
code_availability: All JCM code and associated data is available in the public repository, linked on JCM's doi page at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18189579 (Davenport et al., 2026b). The JCM and SPEEDY outputs and modified SPEEDY.f90 code used to generate figures 1, 2, 3 and 4 is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18334906 (Davenport et al., 2026a). Documentation is available at https://jax-gcm.readthedocs.io.
testbed_rationale: JCM is explicitly introduced and open-sourced as a modular, differentiable, and GPU/TPU-accelerated intermediate-complexity atmospheric model designed to serve as a benchmark testbed for hybrid physics-ML modeling, online training, and parameter estimation.
pain_points: Absence of gradients and complexity of legacy Fortran code hinder the development and validation of hybrid physics-ML models and parameter tuning.
Offline training of ML parameterizations often leads to instabilities and climate drift when coupled online to dynamical cores.
Traditional Fortran climate models are costly and difficult to port to modern hardware accelerators (GPUs/TPUs).
Existing testbeds are either too simplified (e.g., Lorenz 96) or lack process-based physical parameterization schemes required for mechanistic understanding (e.g., NeuralGCM).
extraction_notes: The paper presents JCM v1.0, coupling the Dinosaur dynamical core with JAX-reimplemented SPEEDY physics. While no neural network is trained in this study, automatic differentiation via JAX (JVP and VJP) is demonstrated for parameter calibration (via gradient descent) and sensitivity analysis.
